supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:29 UTC, the proxy recorded NWD\ivy.chen requesting https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1, with status 200. This is temporally close to the reported PowerShell window.
The request was associated with a successful CONNECT tunnel to raw.githubusercontent.com, and the recorded tunnel transferred data in both directions.

The supplied environment context describes workstation patching as sam.okafor running a script from FILE-NWD-01 while working from WS-SOKAFOR-01; it does not identify Ivy Chen downloading this GitHub script as an authorized workflow.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records show a successful request for the script but do not include its contents, hash, or repository commit, so its purpose and safety cannot be assessed.
The supplied records do not show a PowerShell process creation or command line, nor establish that the requested script was saved or executed.
The evidence provided does not establish whether the GitHub path is an authorized Northwind tool or whether Ivy Chen intentionally initiated the request.
claims_not_established: That PowerShell actually ran on WS-ICHEN-01 during the alert window.
That u.ps1 was malicious, benign, or the cause of the reported PowerShell window.
That the GitHub repository or script is an approved organizational resource.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint process and PowerShell operational logs for WS-ICHEN-01 around 13:40 UTC, including command lines, parent processes, and script-block or module logging if available.
Endpoint file-system evidence for a downloaded or executed u.ps1, including file path, timestamps, and hash.
Proxy inspection or GitHub repository evidence sufficient to recover the requested script contents and verify its repository, commit, and organizational authorization.
Confirmation from the relevant IT owner or change/ticket records whether Ivy Chen was expected to retrieve or run this script.
unrelated_findings: A Dropbox updater ran as SYSTEM on WS-ICHEN-01; Dropbox is not among the services listed as approved, but these records do not show a file-sharing or upload action. Triage separately. (T033-00210, T033-00211)

Kerberos records show the leo.martins account requesting tickets from WS-ICHEN-01, followed by a network logon for leo.martins to WS-NBLAKE-01 from that workstation's IP. This is outside the alerted activity and merits separate review. (T033-00237, T033-00238, T033-00249)
